newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt dives in late trade, hit by U.S.
newsitem.headline: German debt dives in late trade, hit by U.S.

text.p: German Bunds took a swift trip south in late trade on Friday as jitters in U.S. credit markets fed through to Germany and sparked what traders described as panic selling.

With a long Pentecost weekend ahead in Germany, dealers said investors were scrambling to square off positions, wary that a meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy setting meeting on Tuesday might lead to an interest rate rise.
"People are afraid that the U.S. market will weaken again on Monday on rate rise fears and we will not be able to react to it," said one Frankfurt-based trader.
By 1518 GMT, the DTB June future was 48 basis points lower on the day at 101.86, having crashed through key technical supports, falling from a session high at 102.65.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was offering a bid yield of 5.764 percent at a price of 101.72 bid with the German market being outclassed by Treasuries on spreads.
The 10-year yield gap stood at 103 basis points in late European trade compared with 109 at the previous close.
"People are either locking in profits in futures or liquidating their positions before the weekend," another trader said.
Having traded in firmer ground for most of the session, the June Bund future shed around 50 ticks in heavy selling pressure between around 1400 and 1430 GMT, traders said.

After Monday's German bank holiday, the June contract will again be at the mercy of the U.S. markets, but should find support in the 101.42 region where it plotted a low on daily charts on May 2, analysts said.
U.S. economists are split 50/50 on whether the Fed will move to tighten monetary policy at its meeting on Tuesday after it raised the Fed funds rate by a quarter point in March.
